sentences.text: This petition was called on for hearing today.

Coram :
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Surya Kant
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Dipankar Datta

For Petitioner(s) Mr. Venkita Subramoniam T.R, AOR  Mr. Rahat Bansal, Adv.
 Mr. Likhichand Bonsle, Adv.
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.

The petitioner filed a writ petition before the High Court seeking following reliefs:
A. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus, commanding the respondent no.2 to decide the representation of petitioner dated 21.9.2022 (contained in Annexure-1 to the writ petition), within time specified by this Honble Court.

B. Issue a writ of mandamus commanding respondent to pass necessary order for de-notification of the property in question under Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Nagina Devi vs State Of U.P. on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133035891/
1 Act within a time specified by this Honble Court. 17:24:02 IST Reason:
2.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Nagina Devi vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The aforesaid writ petition has been dismissed by the High Court vide impugned order pointing out inter alia that nowhere the petitioner has put her claim in respect of compensation or that the actual possession of the land was not taken.
3. We have gone through the averments made in the writ petition filed by the petitioner.

It appears from the contents of paragraphs 6 and 7 of the writ petition that the petitioner attempted to build her case within the four-corners of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 2013 Act),
but no such contention appears to have been raised before the High Court when the matter was heard.
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the absence of any detailed factual foundation, it would not be expedient for this Court to express any opinion.

The special leave petition is, accordingly, dismissed at this stage with liberty to the petitioner to move a review application before the High Court, if so advised along with specific details, if any, to make out a case in terms of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
5. All pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

(ARJUN BISHT) (PREETHI T.C.)
COURT MASTER (SH) COURT MASTER (NSH)
